title: Record an explicit notification route for standalone launcher runs and document restart-safe launch forms
outcome: A standalone launcher can retain a genuine recorded completion route without host test-run registration. Existing recover settles an interrupted standalone run and notifies that recorded recipient without rerunning it; launch documentation explains which forms can survive a host restart and why an unregistered run with no route cannot notify GO-only owners.
acceptance: A standalone launcher invocation can deliberately record one completion recipient using the genuine inherited notification identity while opting out of host test-run registration. The saved request identifies the originating sender and exact recipient; missing/partial identity, self-send and a later recovery attempt under a different sender cannot invent or take over that route.

When a recorded standalone run is recovered after its launcher and recorded command owners have exited, existing recover settlement preserves completed stages and terminal-write races, marks interrupted work unknown rather than passed, and sends one run-named interruption/completion notice to the saved recipient under its stable key. Repeated recovery or notification does not rerun stages or duplicate delivered mail; a send failure leaves the saved result and retryable notification intact. A surviving worker is not recovered as interrupted.

Behavioural tests cover the standalone route without registration, recovery and idempotent notification, missing or substituted sender refusal, notification transport failure, and a surviving worker control. docs/test.md explains harness background versus detached launch lifetimes, the supported notification-only standalone form, and that a hostless unregistered run with no recorded recipient cannot be automatically discovered or notify owners named only in GO prose.
